title: Application for bail at the police station
ruleSource: Written from S.A Badmus' Criminal Litigation drafts (Lawdeck knowledge base). To be confirmed by the legal reviewer, including every statutory provision cited.

parts.why: The letterhead: the sender's name, address and contacts at the top. Source: Criminal Litigation drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

References come before the date; leave them blank if none was given. Letters are dated; notices and resolutions carry their date at the end. Source: Criminal Litigation drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).
The addressee's name or office and address, before the salutation. Source: Criminal Litigation drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).
The salutation. Source: Criminal Litigation drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).
The subject heading. Source: Criminal Litigation drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

parts.text:
We are solicitors to {{suspect}} of {{suspectAddress}}, who was arrested on {{arrestDate}} on the allegation of {{offence}}, and has been detained in your custody since then.

We apply for the bail of our client pending the conclusion of your investigation, under {{policeBailProvision}}.

Our client undertakes to report at the station, and to appear in any court, whenever his presence is required. He is ready to comply with any terms or conditions of bail that may be imposed.

Thank you for your anticipated cooperation.
parts.why: The body: who you act for, when and why the client was arrested (name the offence, not just the act), how long the client has been held, the law the application is brought under, and an undertaking to comply with the conditions of bail. Do not offer a surety yet: the terms of bail have not been given. Source: Criminal Litigation drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

The complimentary close, the signature space, and the name and capacity of the person signing. Always sign a draft in the exam. Source: Criminal Litigation drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

fields.label: Sender
fields.question: Who is the letter from? The law firm, company or person, as it appears on the letterhead.

fields.label: Sender's address and contacts
fields.question: The sender's address, email and phone number for the letterhead.

fields.label: Date of the letter
fields.question: What date should the letter bear? Use a date close to the facts, never after the exam date.

fields.label: Addressee
fields.question: Who is the letter to? Give the name or office, for example The Divisional Police Officer.

fields.label: Capacity of the person signing
fields.question: In what capacity do they sign? For example: Principal Partner, Company Secretary.

fields.label: Client
fields.question: Who is the client in custody? Give the full name.

fields.label: Offence alleged
fields.question: What offence is alleged? Name the offence, for example grievous bodily harm.

fields.label: Law relied on
fields.question: Which provisions of the Constitution and the Police Act or the ACJL/ACJA do you rely on? Check them in the library.
